title: Proposal (ZIFFER-SPEC-001 §3, B-1a / B-6 / SR-5 / V-11; canonical form §9.2, RFC 8785)
description:
The typed candidate operation the Policy Engine decides over (§3), and the hash preimage every other artifact in this system binds to. Carried on legs F1.3, F4.1, F4.2 and F5.2 of the leg register (ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 Annex A).

ONE SCHEMA, NOT TWO, AND THE CANONICAL FLAG IS AN ENCODING RULE RATHER THAN A PROPERTY. The closed artifact vocabulary carries two names for this object -- `Proposal` (§3) and `canonical Proposal` (B-1a) -- and they are one field set. `canonical` names an ENCODING of these bytes, not a second artifact with a second shape: B-1a requires the Proposal reaching the Executor to be `canonicalized identically before hashing`, and identical canonicalization of two different field sets is not a thing that can be asked for. A `canonical_proposal.schema.json` beside this file would put two definitions on one object, which is the defect this repository has published corrections for three times. The flag is therefore stated once, here, in the ENCODING paragraph below -- and NOT as a property. A field asserting `I am canonical` would be the party under verification certifying its own encoding; B-1a's obligation is discharged by the receiver hashing what it actually received (9.3-3), never by reading a claim about it.

ENCODING: JCS, AND IT MUST NOT BE MIXED WITH THE CBOR RULE. §9.2 states the split in one sentence -- RFC 8785 (JCS) for the Proposal, canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 §4.2) for the receipt and the Attestation Object (WE-1/WE-2, AT-8a). AT-8a writes the second half as a prohibition (`JCS MUST NOT be used for the Attestation Object`) and this schema writes the first half the same way: canonical CBOR MUST NOT be used for the Proposal. Mixing them is the encoding split at the point it does the most damage, because `proposal_hash` is not one artifact's identifier -- it is the binding EVERY other artifact carries. AT-1 puts it in the object the humans sign; 9.3-3 makes the Executor recompute it over what it will actually execute; DS-6a builds `action_id` from it and DS-6f pins an IMMUTABLE `proposal_hash -> origin_nonce` binding in the Consumption Ledger, retained INDEFINITELY because an expiring one would reopen Z3 (CL-3, CL-4); DR-13 writes it into the notice. Two encoders therefore do not merely disagree about a digest. They give ONE action two identities. The quorum the humans raised binds to a hash the Executor never computes, so 9.3-3 fails closed and at the verifier that is indistinguishable from a forgery -- the sentence WE-4's rationale already had to write once, for a type nobody had written down. And a re-drive re-encoded by the second encoder presents a `proposal_hash` DS-6f holds no binding for, so the recovery path DS-3 mandates fails closed on an authorized action; an implementation that instead BINDS the new hash has silently given one action two action identities and two DS-6b idempotency keys, which is the doubled trade DS-4 names as the worst failure available. Y5.2/AT-8a is that hazard one artifact over, against a binding kept for 24 hours; this one is kept forever.

THE FIELD SET IS PR-1's (v1.3.27), AND THIS SCHEMA IS ITS RENDERING. Through v1.3.26 ZIFFER-SPEC-001 STATED NO FIELD SET FOR THE PROPOSAL: §3 defined it in one sentence, SR-5 required the `(schema_id, schema_version, schema_hash)` triple and the fidelity class, B-6 forbade the client to set the stamp, V-11 spoke of an `envelope` and its `payload` and put `task_type` inside the payload -- and `reference/src/acp_executor.py` read a THIRD shape, flat, with `tenant_id`, `targets`, `params` and `cidrs` at top level and no `schema_version`, `schema_hash` or `fidelity` at all. Three shapes, one artifact, and `proposal_hash` was a hash over whichever one an implementer chose. This file reported that choosing between them was a normative act and refused to make it. v1.3.27 made it, after the first end-to-end build (M7) put the two shapes on one wire: the door emitted this envelope, the verifier graded the flat object, §9.3 step 8 looked for a `tenant_id` the envelope could not carry, and neither side could be called wrong. PR-1 fixes the envelope -- the triple, the fidelity class, the tenant the admitting adapter's VERIFIED bundle names, and a CLOSED payload of `task_type`, `operator`, `targets`, `params` and `cidrs` -- as the one Proposal, the one hash preimage, and the one object §8.3.1's typing environment is derived from. The flat shape is gone: the reference reads the envelope through one accessor, `acp_executor.payload()`, and the Rust verifier through `acp_decision::Proposal::from_wire`, so a second reading has nowhere to live.

WHY BOTH LEVELS ARE CLOSED, AND WHAT THAT REFUSES. `additionalProperties` is false at the root AND at the payload, and every property at both levels is REQUIRED -- `params` and `cidrs` may be EMPTY objects, never absent. An optional field means one object has two valid encodings and therefore two `proposal_hash` values -- Z4, which AT-8b closes for the Attestation Object by making its field set closed and every field required. Until v1.3.27 no clause did the same for the Proposal, although it is hashed, bound and ledger-keyed by the same machinery and its DS-6f binding is the one retained indefinitely; PR-1 now states AT-8b's rule for it in as many words, and this schema is where the rule is machine-readable. One consequence is disclosed rather than resolved: §7.4 permits a deployment to insert a domain-screening stage whose verdict `enters the Proposal as a field policy can rule on`. V-1 forbids unknown fields on the registered Input Schema that governs `params`, and PR-1 closes the payload around it, so that verdict has no key to live under. The specification names the field, does not name its key, does not type it, and does not say whether it is inside the hash preimage. A deployment that inserts a screen is outside this schema and needs a version increment, on AT-8b's reasoning applied here.

WHAT IS NOT A FIELD. `proposal_hash` is DERIVED, not carried, and has no property below. It is SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of these bytes (§9.2), and §9.3 step 3 makes the Executor hash `the Proposal the Executor independently received and canonicalized` -- `never whatever the receipt describes`. A Proposal carrying its own hash invites a reader to compare a transmitted value against a transmitted value, which is TR-10 exactly: a transmitted identifier is a NAME for a binding, not evidence of one. Also absent, each deliberately: `risk_level` and `reversibility`, recomputed by the Executor from the signed bundle and these bytes (TR-8, RV-3) because a receipt-asserted risk is X1 and a receipt-asserted reversibility is the same defect with a new field; and `origin_nonce` and `idempotency_key`, pinned by the ledger with any receipt-carried claim diagnostic only (DS-6f, Z3). `operator` IS a field since PR-1 -- it is what §8.4 step 4 checks capability for -- and it is still not authority at floor-HIGH, where the value the Executor acts on is `attestations[].obj.operator` inside the attester signature (Y4, §9.3 step 7b(iii-a)).

SUITE 12 CLASSIFICATION. Every property below is class T at the schema layer: this document constrains SHAPE, and shape is not authority. What discharges each one lives elsewhere and is cited on the property rather than restated (DP-84). The triple is a NAME for a binding until §8.4 step 1 verifies it against the SIGNED registry (TR-10, SR-2). `fidelity` is RECOMPUTED from the bundle-registered adapter binding for `schema_id` (TR-8, §9.3 step 7) and is never read as authority from here, notwithstanding that B-6 requires it to be carried. `tenant_id` is stamped by the adapter from the bundle it VERIFIED (PR-2) -- B at the door -- and is T on the wire until §9.3 step 8 compares it against the receipt's and against the bundle the Executor trusts, at which point a receipt, a Proposal and a manifest that all name one tenant is what the step establishes. `operator` below floor-HIGH is the disclosed residual the receipt's `operator` already was (ACP-CLASS-001); at floor-HIGH it is B through Y4.

schema_id.description:
Names the registered schema the payload was validated against. Schemas are content-addressed by `schema_id` + `schema_version` + `schema_hash` (SR-1) and SR-5 requires that triple on every Proposal. It is also the key the Executor uses to look up the bundle-registered ADAPTER binding when it recomputes `fidelity` (§9.3 step 7), so a Proposal without it leaves TR-8 with nothing to recompute against and the FC-2 confirmation requirement resting on a transmitted stamp.

THE PATTERN IS §6.3's, CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, AND THE REFERENCE DOES NOT SATISFY IT. `reference/suites/conformance.py` builds `schema_id: "fw.v1"`, and `.` is outside that class. The pattern is kept as written: widening a schema's own pattern to admit the fixture that violates it proves only that the instrument is adjustable. Whether a pattern stated inside a NORMATIVE EXAMPLE binds an implementation is itself unresolved and is reported, not assumed.

schema_version.description: The semantic version of that registered schema (SR-1), carried on the Proposal by SR-5 so the artifact says which admissible SET it was checked against and not merely which schema name. This is the axis SR-3 decides change direction over: a change is NARROWING only where the new admissible set is a provable subset of the old in every dimension of the bounded lattice -- character class, length bound, enum set, numeric range -- and anything not provably narrowing in every dimension is widening and takes the distinct-reviewer path. v1.2.0 left `narrowing` undefined, which let a net-widening change self-classify as narrowing and bypass review.

schema_hash.description: The content address of that schema version (SR-1), and the reason the triple is a triple rather than a pair: `schema_id` and `schema_version` are names a registry could remap, a hash is not. Class T here and a NAME for a binding, not evidence of one (TR-10). The binding is discharged at §8.4 step 1 -- schema attestation, valid `(schema_id, version, hash)` in bundle, else DENY -- against the SIGNED registry, and the validator MUST refuse to start on a signature or hash mismatch (SR-2). SR-6 supplies the other direction: a Proposal naming a removed schema receives DENY with `schema_retired`.

fidelity.description:
The fidelity class of the adapter that produced this Proposal. Stamped by the ADAPTER, bound into the Decision and the receipt, and MUST NOT be settable by the client (B-6); carried here because B-6 and SR-5 both say the Proposal carries it.

CARRIED IS NOT TRUSTED. The Executor MUST verify fidelity against the bundle-registered adapter binding for this `schema_id` and MUST NOT accept it as transmitted (TR-8, §9.3 step 7), because a forged `F-HIGH` stamp suppresses the FC-2 confirmation requirement exactly as v1.3.0's forged `risk_level_floor_only` suppressed attestation (X1). The value is inside the hash preimage, so it is bound to everything `proposal_hash` binds -- including the object the attesters signed and the `resource.effective_tier` comparisons that read `fidelity` in §8.3's own reference bundle -- and it is still not authority for any control decision.

AND NO CLAUSE SAYS WHAT A DISAGREEMENT HERE MEANS. §9.3 step 7a makes a disagreement between the recomputed value and the RECEIPT's value a critical alert. Nothing states the outcome when the recomputed value disagrees with the value carried in the PROPOSAL, which is the value AT-3 showed the attesters and the one the quorum is bound to. The Python reference never reaches the question: its Proposal carries no `fidelity` field at all, which is B-6 and SR-5 unimplemented rather than a reading of them.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the admitting Ingress Adapter's VERIFIED bundle governs (RAD-5's value, the manifest's `tenant_id`), stamped by the adapter under PR-2 and never settable by the client -- B-6's rule for `fidelity`, applied to the second value the door supplies. It exists so that §9.3 step 8 has a byte to compare: the step requires the receipt's tenant to equal the Proposal's AND the trusted bundle's, both held independently of the receipt, and until v1.3.27 the schema-shaped Proposal carried no tenant at all, so a conformant door's output could not pass a conformant Executor's step 8. Class T on the wire, discharged at step 8 -- and NOT a lookup key: the Executor selects its bundle from its own configuration and compares this value against it, never the other way round, because a transmitted tenant that selected the policy would be the KMS's pre-RAD-5 defect one component over.

payload.description: The validated object itself: PR-1's closed payload of `task_type`, `operator`, `targets`, `params` and `cidrs`, all five REQUIRED. V-11 is the clause that names both halves -- it requires the validator to reject any envelope whose payload `task_type` disagrees with its `schema_id`. §8.3.1 says the typing environment risk expressions resolve against is `derived from the Proposal schema`: since PR-1 that environment is `params` (each entry an EL-2 value, bound under its own name) together with each target's tier from `floors.json` (`<target>.effective_tier`, RK-2), and nothing else in the envelope is visible to a rule.

schema_id.description:
The identifier half of SR-1's content address, carried on every Proposal by SR-5 and on the receipt that decided it by §9.2.

ONE DECLARATION, AND WHY IT IS NOT SHARED WITH `task_type`. Before ACP-78 M1 this pattern was written out three times in this root: here, on the receipt, and on the payload's `task_type`, which is a DIFFERENT value that happens to share a character class. The first two are one type and are now one declaration. The third is deliberately left as its own inline pattern, because V-11 requires `task_type` to `agree with` `schema_id` and does not say what agreement is -- string identity, or a registry lookup. Giving both fields one type would answer V-11 by writing a schema, which is the move this root exists to refuse. Two types with the same pattern are two types; one type with two declarations is the defect.

THE PATTERN IS §6.3's, CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, AND THE REFERENCE DOES NOT SATISFY IT: `reference/suites/conformance.py` builds `schema_id: "fw.v1"` and `.` is outside the class. It is kept as written, because widening a schema's own pattern to admit the fixture that violates it proves only that the instrument is adjustable. Whether a pattern stated inside a NORMATIVE EXAMPLE binds an implementation at all is unresolved and reported rather than assumed.

schema_version.description:
The version half of SR-1's content address (SR-5), declared once here and `$ref`d by the receipt, which carries the same triple. It is the axis SR-3 decides change direction over: a change is NARROWING only where the new admissible set is a provable subset of the old in EVERY dimension of the bounded lattice -- character class, length bound, enum set, numeric range -- and anything not provably narrowing in every dimension is widening and takes the distinct-reviewer path. v1.2.0 left `narrowing` undefined, which let a net-widening change self-classify as narrowing and bypass review.

The pattern is §6.3's and carries the same unresolved question as `schema_id`: it is stated inside a section titled `Reference Schemas (Normative Examples)`, and whether an example binds is not settled anywhere.

proposal_payload.description:
`task_type` and the four fields PR-1 closes the payload around. CLOSED at this level since v1.3.27, and the registered Input Schema's fields live INSIDE `params`, where V-1 closes them.

WHAT WAS OPEN HERE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ANY MORE. Through v1.3.26 this object declared `task_type` and left everything else undeclared, on the argument that the payload's field set is closed SOMEWHERE ELSE -- the per-tenant, content-addressed registry SR-1 and L-06 describe, a DEPLOYMENT fact this file must not restate. The argument stands, and PR-1 relocates it one level down: the registered schema governs `params`, an object whose keys are the deployment's, while the four members every Proposal has in common -- the action class, the principal, the resources, the CIDR widths -- are named once, here, and REQUIRED. An open payload had left the verifier no way to tell a registered field from a smuggled one, and the generated types carried `task_type` and nothing else, which a reader could take for the whole payload (ACP-153, item 14).

Z4, SAID PLAINLY. Every member REQUIRED and both objects closed is AT-8b's rule -- no optional fields, no defaultable fields, no extension points -- applied to the Proposal, which through v1.3.26 had no counterpart of it. `params` and `cidrs` are EMPTY objects when an action has none, never absent, so one action has one encoding. What this cannot close: a registered Input Schema that declares an optional or defaulted field inside `params` reopens it there, and no clause forbids one from doing so; B-1a is what stops that becoming two hashes -- the CANONICAL Proposal travels to the Executor and §9.3 step 3 hashes what arrived -- and the absence of an AT-8b-style rule for registered schemas is reported, not assumed harmless.

WHAT THIS TYPE ENFORCES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. EL-2: every `params` value is an integer or a string, and a value of any other JSON type -- a non-integer number, a boolean, null, an array, an object, or an integer outside the width the deployment declares under AC-1a -- MUST cause the Proposal to be REFUSED, never re-typed and never coerced. Since v1.3.27 the generated types carry that domain (`param_value`), so an off-domain value fails to parse rather than being read as a string; the clause exists because a JSON `22.0` bound as a STRING in the Python reference graded MEDIUM where `port: 22` graded HIGH, against this document's own reference bundle. Not enforced here and enforced at the validator instead: V-7 (NFC before pattern matching, bidi and zero-width code points refused), V-6 (duplicate keys refused at every depth), L-01 to L-05 (32 KiB before parsing, depth 8, 24 fields per schema, 2,048 characters per string, 100 items per list), and V-1's closure of `params` against the registered schema -- for which no signed registry exists yet in the bundle (ACP-153, item 12).

task_type.description:
The action class: a `Literal` over the registered set, closed world, no dynamic dispatch and no plugins (V-8). §8.4 step 3 looks up a risk function by it and DENIES where none exists -- an action with no risk function is refused at `8.4-3` rather than graded HIGH, because grading an unknown action is P-4's rule broken. RV-3 recomputes the reversibility class from the trusted bundle and THIS value, never from the receipt, and RV-1's absent-implies-IRREVERSIBLE default keys on it; DR-13 then reads that default on the fast path, which is what turned it from documentation into a control.

V-11 REQUIRES IT TO AGREE WITH `schema_id` AND DOES NOT SAY WHAT AGREEMENT IS. The clause admits two readings -- string identity, or a lookup resolving `schema_id` to the task type it registers -- and the two disagree on this repository's own fixtures, which pair `schema_id: "fw.v1"` with `task_type: "modify_firewall_rule"`. §6.3's normative example implements identity (`v.task_type != info.data["schema_id"]`), under which these are two spellings of one value and this property is redundant with `schema_id` -- and V-11 exists precisely because two spellings can disagree. The pattern below is `schema_id`'s, for that reason and no stronger one: no clause states a pattern for `task_type` directly, and this is the strongest thing the text supports.

operator.description: The operating principal the action is proposed for: the identity §8.4 step 4 checks every required capability against, step 6 tests against the excluded roles, and §8.5 groups accumulators by. The Attestation Object's `operator_id`, referenced rather than re-declared: one definition of a principal identifier. CARRIED IS NOT TRUSTED. Below floor-HIGH this is the disclosed residual the receipt's `operator` already was -- a client-asserted principal, bounded by the capability check that binds it to signed entitlements (§8.8). At floor-HIGH the authoritative value is `attestations[].obj.operator` inside every attester signature (Y4, §9.3 step 7b(iii-a)), and the Policy Engine copies THIS value into the object the attesters sign, so a Proposal whose `operator` differs from what the quorum attested cannot execute.

targets.description: The resources the action names, by the identifiers `floors.json` is keyed by (RK-1; the item bounds are that table's `propertyNames`). At least one: an action that names no resource has no floor to recompute a risk from, and TR-8 has nothing to recompute against -- refused at the door under this schema rather than graded against nothing. At most 100 (L-05's per-list bound). Each target's tier enters the typing environment as `<target>.effective_tier` (RK-2), and a target absent from `floors.json` resolves to `T3` (RK-1) -- unknown is never LOW.

propertyNames.description: A parameter name as the registered Input Schema declares it and as a rule names it in an expression (§8.3.1): lower-case, underscores, at most 64 characters. The set of names is the REGISTERED schema's (SR-1, V-1), closed there and not here.

params.description: The registered Input Schema's object -- the fields `(schema_id, schema_version, schema_hash)` resolves to and V-1 closes -- carried under one key so the four common members beside it can be named without restating a per-tenant registry here. Each value is an EL-2 value (`param_value`): an integer or a string, bound into the typing environment under its own name. EMPTY, never absent, for an action with no parameters (Z4). Nothing in this repository validates a payload against a registered Input Schema, because no signed registry exists in the bundle yet (ACP-153, item 12): until it does, `params` is closed by name at the registry a deployment holds and open to this file, which is disclosed rather than papered over.

propertyNames.description: The name of the CIDR-typed parameter the width belongs to, in the same class as a `params` name.

cidrs.description: Prefix widths of the CIDR-typed parameters, by parameter name: `{"source_cidr": 24}` for a `/24`. §8.3.1's `prefix_len(...)` reads them, and the environment builder binds each as `<name>.prefix_len` (AC-1a's integer width). A width is 0..128; an IPv4 width above 32 is the registered schema's to refuse. EMPTY, never absent, for an action with no CIDR parameter. Carried apart from `params` rather than parsed out of a string there, because the width is what a rule compares and a rule that had to parse a CIDR would be a rule that could be made to parse it wrongly.

param_value.description: EL-2's value domain: an integer or a string, and nothing else. A rule's environment binds each `params` entry to one of these; a value of any other JSON type -- a non-integer number, a boolean, null, an array, an object -- MUST refuse the whole Proposal (EL-2, closes the v1.3.17 `22`/`22.0` defect). The integer is bounded by the width the deployment declares under AC-1a; the generated types carry `i64`, and a value above it is out of the domain rather than merely large.
